tests.name: Effective description
tests.reasoning: The description uses imperative phrasing ('Use this skill when...'), focuses on user-facing symptoms (slow, throttled, silent endpoints) rather than internal implementation, explicitly lists many trigger contexts including cases where terminology isn't named directly ('even if they do not mention cold start, provisioned concurrency...'), and while dense, it stays as a focused paragraph covering the scope comprehensively.
tests.evidence: Use this skill when a serverless endpoint is slow or throttled after idle periods, its MaxConcurrency is rejected or exhausted, or its creation fails validation on an option a real-time endpoint accepts; ... even if they do not mention cold start, provisioned concurrency, SNS topics, InputLocation, backlog scaling or AsyncInferenceConfig by name.

tests.name: Verbosity and conciseness
tests.reasoning: The body stays focused on SageMaker serverless/async-specific concepts (ServerlessConfig, MaxConcurrency, NotificationConfig, ApproximateBacklogSizePerInstance) and does not explain general concepts the agent already knows. It is dense but each section carries domain-specific, non-obvious information.
tests.evidence: "Reports serverless cold-start latency — a sustained high ModelSetupTime with no Provisioned Concurrency configured on the ServerlessConfig."

tests.name: Detailed reference materials must not be in body
tests.reasoning: The body keeps the check table to a compact index ('what-it-catches') and explicitly defers full detection rules, remediations, and citations to references/checks-sagemaker-serverless-async.md. No large reference blocks or embedded lookup tables with full data are in the body.
tests.evidence: "The full six-column detection rules, remediations, and citations live in the reference — the table below is a what-it-catches index."

tests.name: Reference files must be linked
tests.reasoning: Every file under references/ is linked via markdown links in the body (checks-sagemaker-serverless-async.md, collection-reference.md, api-quirks.md, metrics-and-logs.md, cloudwatch-alarm-reference.md, known-causes.md).

tests.name: Reference links must specify when to load
tests.reasoning: Each reference link is accompanied by a clear trigger condition for when to load it, e.g. tied to symptoms in the Router table or specific steps.
tests.evidence: "Load [known-causes.md](references/known-causes.md) whenever the user names an error or symptom; match it to a section, check the cited AWS page, and give the cause, how to confirm it, and the fix."

tests.name: Reference path format
tests.reasoning: All reference links use relative paths rooted at references/ with no absolute paths or traversal.

tests.name: Prescription vs description
tests.reasoning: Fragile operations (guardrails, validation gate, severity rules) are highly prescriptive with explicit non-negotiable rules, while flexible areas (break-fix diagnosis, router matching) explain reasoning and allow judgment, matching prescriptiveness to fragility.
tests.evidence: "Non-negotiable, at every step: 1. Read-only. Never call CreateEndpoint..."

tests.name: Defaults, not menus
tests.reasoning: The skill doesn't present competing tools/approaches as equal menu choices; it consistently points to one reference file per symptom type via the Router table, acting as defaults rather than listing alternatives.
tests.evidence: Router table maps each symptom to one specific API call and reference, not multiple equal options.

tests.name: Favor procedures over declarations
tests.reasoning: The skill teaches a generalizable diagnostic approach (symptom matching, confirm via collection calls, report with check-id) rather than a one-off instance; the Review Procedure and Router generalize across any serverless/async endpoint scenario.
tests.evidence: "Match the symptom, confirm with the collection calls, then report with the check-id and severity from the catalog."

tests.name: Gotchas section
tests.reasoning: The skill has both a 'Common wrong answers' section (functioning as gotchas) and an 'Error Handling' section documenting non-obvious traps like misleading InService state and absent datapoints.
tests.evidence: "'The async endpoint is InService, so it is serving and the queue is fine.' InService is control-plane state. An async or serverless variant can be InService with CurrentInstanceCount = 0..."

tests.reasoning: The skill provides an explicit health report template referenced in assets/ for structured output when a full report is requested.

tests.name: Asset files must be linked

tests.name: Asset links must specify when to load

tests.name: Validation loops
tests.reasoning: The skill includes an explicit self-validation gate section instructing the agent to re-check its output (check-ids, observed values, severities, no secrets) before presenting.
tests.evidence: "Before presenting, re-check your output against this list. Treat it as a gate, not a suggestion."
